 EL PASO, Texas (KFOX14/CBS4) — With runoff elections approaching, the El Paso County Elections Department is testing its election equipment to make sure systems are ready for voters.
 Election officials said the testing is designed to confirm voter information is correctly loaded into election systems, that voting machines are working properly, and that ballots are correctly assigned to voters. 
 Organizers said the process is meant to ensure accuracy and prepare ballots for the upcoming elections.
 RELATED: El Paso District 1 City Rep race headed to runoff: Chavez vs. Armijo 
 "Test ballots from 64 precincts will be used to verify that the pollbook equipment is properly programmed," said Melissa Martin with the El Paso County Elections Department. "Once marked, the ballot will be printed and cast on the tabulating machine so that everything that comes out of the elections warehouse is prepared for early voting and election day."
 Early voting for runoff elections in El Paso starts on Nov. 30 and ends on Dec. 8.

 There will be 12 early voting locations serving the city's Districts 1, 6 and 8.
